newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Air Ukraine passenger volume falls in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Air Ukraine passenger volume falls in 1996.

text.p: State-owned Air Ukraine's passenger numbers fell sharply to just over one million in 1996, a senior aviation official said on Monday.
Volodymyr Boyko, head of the Aviation Department's economic unit, told Reuters that Air Ukraine carried 1.06 million passengers last year compared to 1.27 million the year before.
But one official at the flag carrier told Reuters the volume of passengers on international flights had risen to 700,000 from about 500,000.
"The decline in passenger volume was due to the growing number of tiny regional air companies, most of which have only one leased plane," the official said. "They grabbed passengers."
He said there were up to 100 air companies in Ukraine.
The official refused to give company profit figures for last year but said Air Ukraine had paid 17.5 million hryvnias (about $1 million) in tax.
Boyko said Air Ukraine planned to carry no fewer passengers in 1997 than last year.
Air Ukraine has 250 Soviet-made planes, including Illyushin-62s, Tupolev-130 and 154s, Yakovlev-40 and 42s and Antonov-24 jets.

The company flies to some European destinations, as well as North America, the Middle East, China, India and southeast Asia. It is Ukraine's major carrier on internal routes and to points in the former Soviet Union.
Air Ukraine wants to lease this year either Boeing or Airbus aircraft for North American routes.
Government officials have said the results of the tender between the U.S. and western European aeroplane manufacturers would be announced later this week.
